 Oral Judgment :
1.

In the present matter, the office note shows that non- applicant No.2 was duly served, however
due to her non- appearance counsel Mrs R.P. Godbole, was appointed by the Court.

But no one
appeared o
n behalf of the non-applicant No.2 in the morning session.
Hence, the matter was taken up in the afternoon session, but again, when the matter was called out, no one appeared on behalf of non-applicant No.2 in the matter.

Therefore, this Court proceeded to decide the matter in absence of non- applicant No.2.
2.
Heard. Rule.
Rule made returnable forthwith.
By consent of the applicants and non-applicant No.1, the application is taken up for final hearing at the stage of admission.

3. By this application, the applicants are praying to quash and set aside the proceedings of Regular Criminal Case No. 2364 of 2025 arising out of Crime No. 1726 of 2021 registered with Police Station Frezarpura, District Amravati, and Charge-sheet bearing No.439 of 2025 dated 28/11/2025, for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(n), 417, 504, and 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

4. In short, the case of the prosecution is that present non- applicant No.2, on 11/10/2021, lodged a complaint at the police station alleging that one Prashant Bhimrao Moon, under the rkn 3 10 apl623.2022.odt pretext of marriage, developed physical relationship with her.
However, when the complainant asked him to perform the marriage, he was avoiding the same.
Therefore, on 09/10/2021, she went to the house of Prashant.
At that time, the present applicants, who are the father, mother and brother of the Prashant, allegedly abused her in filthy language and made several allegations against her.
On the basis of these allegations, offences punishable under Section 376(2)(n), 417, 504 and 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, were registered against the present applicants.
5. It is an admitted fact that present application is moved by the father, mother, and brother of the main accused Prashant.
From the entire report and the statements, which are recorded by the Investigating Officer, there are no averments which attract Section 376(2)(n) against the present applicants.
Therefore, prima-facie Section 376(2)(n) is not attracted in the matter.
6. In the present matter, during the course of arguments, the learned APP has also admitted the fact that, offence punishable under Section 376(2)(n) is not attracted against the present applicants.
Therefore, the offence registered against the present applicants under Section 376 is prima-facie illegal in the matter.
7. It is further pertinent to note that the offence is also registered under Section 417 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 against the present applicants.

Here again, from the prosecution story, it is clear that no allegations are made of cheating against rkn 4 10 apl623.2022.odt the present applicants in Smt. sentences.text: All the allegations of cheating are against the main accused Prashant.
Therefore, on this count also, the offence punishable under Section 417 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, is not prima-facie attracted against the present applicants in the matter.
8. The only allegations against the applicants are that when the complainant visited the house of Prashant on 09/10/2021, she was abused in filthy language by the present applicants.
Therefore, the offence under Sections 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 can be said to be added against applicants.
Therefore, this Court is required to consider whether prima-facie, offence under Sections 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 is made out against applicants.

9. In this regard, it is necessary to note down that there are no specific averments either in the FIR nor in the statement of the complainant, that when Prashant was avoiding to meet her and not attending her telephone, what was reason for her to went alone to the house of Prashant.

Normally,
in such cases, the complainant would have been accompanied by elder family members if she really wanted to meet the family members of the applicant.
However, in the present case, the complainant alone went to the house of Prashant.
Furthermore according to complainant herself, when Prashant saw her, he left the house.
If Prashant had left the house, then again question arose why she entered into the house of the applicant.

Therefore, the allegations which are raised against the applicants do not seems to be rkn 5 10 apl623.2022.odt prima-facie trustworthy.
10.

From perusal of the entire record, it is evident that the complainant, being frustrated due to the denial of marriage by Prashant, to built pressure on the Prashant, the allegations are seems to be raised against the present applicants.
Therefore, in my considered opinion, the allegations made against the applicant's family, prima-facie, do not found any substance.
11. It is further pertinent to note that, in the entire investigation, there is no eye-witness to the alleged incident as stated by the complainant in her complaint.
All the statement shows that they were hearsay.
Hence, in absence of any cogent evidence available on record, it will not be proper to drag the present applicants in the criminal process for no fault on their part in the matter.
12. In these circumstances, I am of the opinion that no case is made out by the complainant to drag the present applicants in the alleged crime.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER a] The Criminal Application is allowed.

b] The Regular Criminal Case No. 2364 of 2025 pending on the file of Judicial Magistrate First Class, Amravati, arising out of charge-sheet bearing No. 439 of 2025 dated 28/11/2025 for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(n), 417, 504,
and 506 read with rkn 6 10 apl623.2022.odt Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860, in Crime No. 1726 of 2021, is hereby quashed and set aside, against the present applicants only.
13. Rule is made absolute.
No order as to costs.
